Facility Manager (Remote)

We are seeking an experienced Facility Manager with a strong background in project management to oversee the daily operations, maintenance, and strategic development of our facilities. The ideal candidate will combine hands-on U.S. facility management expertise with proven project management skills to plan, execute, and deliver facility-related projects on time and within budget.

Note: Candidates without prior facility management experience in the United States will not be considered for interview.

Key Responsibilities

Facility Operations

  • Oversee day-to-day operations of the facility, including maintenance, security, cleaning, and vendor management
    •Ensure compliance with U.S. health, safety, and environmental regulations (OSHA and local codes)
    •Manage facility budgets, expenses, and cost-control initiatives
    •Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance schedules

Project Management

  • Plan, initiate, and manage facility improvement, renovation, and relocation projects from start to finish
    •Develop project scopes, timelines, budgets, and resource plans
    •Coordinate with contractors, architects, engineers, and internal stakeholders
    •Track project milestones, identify risks, and implement mitigation strategies
    •Prepare and present project status reports to senior management

Vendor & Contractor Management

  • Source, negotiate, and manage contracts with vendors and service providers
    •Evaluate vendor performance and ensure service level agreements are met

Team Leadership

  • Supervise facility staff, custodial teams, and maintenance personnel
    •Train and mentor team members on safety protocols and best practices

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum 3–5 years of hands-on facility management experience in the United States (required)
    •Demonstrated project management experience (managing budgets, timelines, and cross-functional teams)
    •Strong knowledge of U.S. building codes, OSHA regulations, and building systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing)
    •Proficiency in facility management software and project management tools (e.g., MS Project, Asana, Trello)

Preferred Qualifications

  • PMP certification or equivalent project management training
    •Excellent communication and negotiation skills
    •Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
    •Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously

Work Environment

•Remote

  • Standard schedule: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM US Central Time, Monday–Friday


    •Applicants must have verifiable U.S.-based facility management experience to proceed to interview stage

Join Anywhere Talent and play a pivotal role in empowering businesses with your expertise. Let’s create partnerships that drive success together! Apply now and embark on a rewarding journey with us!

At WelbeHealth, we serve our communities’ most vulnerable seniors through shared intention, pioneering spirit, and the courage to love. These core values and our participant focus lead the way no matter what.

The Senior Facilities Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for WelbeHealth’s facilities portfolio, including new site development, ongoing facility operations, maintenance, vendor performance, equipment and supplies, occupancy services, and financial oversight. This role builds the infrastructure, standards, systems, and team capabilities needed to scale the facilities function as the organization grows. The Senior Facilities Manager creates, owns, and drives consistent enterprise processes, identifies and delivers continuous improvement opportunities, establishes performance measures and governance, and translates business needs into sustainable, repeatable solutions.

This role is different because the Senior Facilities Manager WelbeHealth:

  • Owns the strategy and execution of facilities operations across a growing, multi-state portfolio, building scalable systems, standardized processes, and vendor partnerships that support new market launches and ongoing operational excellence
  • Drives cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement by partnering with market leaders and internal stakeholders to optimize facility performance, manage costs, mitigate operational risks, and deliver safe, reliable, and compliant environments that support our participants and team members

We care about our team members. That’s why we offer:

  • Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
  • Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days
  • 401K savings + match
  • Comprehensive compensation package including base pay and bonus
  • And additional benefits!

On the day-to-day, you will:

  • Lead the facilities function’s operating strategy and translate organizational growth plans into scalable staffing, systems, service-delivery, vendor, and capital requirements, as well as create, own, implement, and continuously improve enterprise facilities policies, standard operating procedures, service level agreements, workflows, controls, and escalation paths
  • Build repeatable and scalable processes that support new market launches, site transitions, and the ongoing operation of a growing multi-state portfolio
  • Own assigned vendor portfolios including but not limited to janitorial, preventative maintenance, linens, hazardous waste disposal, and others as assigned, including ongoing vendor relationship management, creation of service level agreements to meet evolving operational needs, collecting and incorporating feedback from internal WelbeHealth operations leaders, and contract review
  • Own the facilities service request platform and related technology roadmap, including intake, prioritization, assignment, escalation, closure, reporting, and user adoption
  • Use operational data, stakeholder feedback, root-cause analysis, and external best practices to identify improvement opportunities and lead changes that increase quality, speed, consistency, cost effectiveness, and customer experience
  • Define and monitor key performance indicators, service-level expectations, dashboards, and business reviews, communicating risks, trends, decisions, and corrective actions to senior leadership
  • Direct facilities support for multiple market launches, including readiness planning, supply and equipment deployment, vendor activation, training coordination, clinic and kitchen setup, leadership updates, and operational handoff

Job requirements include:

  • Bachelor’s degree in facilities management, construction management, business administration, healthcare administration, engineering, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered
  • Professional certification such as PMP, CFM, FMP, LEED, or related credential preferred
  • Minimum of seven (7) years of progressive experience in facilities, property, construction, or multi-site operations, including at least three years leading teams, programs, or complex cross-functional initiatives
  • Demonstrated success building or scaling a facilities function, service-delivery model, or operating infrastructure in a high-growth organization
  • Proven ability to create, document, implement, and sustain enterprise processes, standards, controls, and governance across multiple locations
  • Experience leading end-to-end process improvement using structured problem-solving, root-cause analysis, change management, and measurable outcome tracking
  • Experience overseeing maintenance, repairs, renovations, new site readiness, vendor services, facilities technology, and operational handoffs across a multi-site portfolio
  • Demonstrated financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, variance management, business-case development, and identification of cost-saving and cost avoidance opportunities
  • Strong vendor and contract management capabilities, including sourcing support, service-level management, performance reviews, issue escalation, and relationship governance

We are seeking a strategic, highly organized, and collaborative Senior Facilities Manager who is passionate about operational excellence, process improvement, and building scalable facilities infrastructure. The ideal candidate brings strong leadership, project management, financial, and vendor management skills, with the ability to oversee multi-site operations, lead new market readiness, manage competing priorities, and drive consistent, cost-effective results. If you thrive in a fast-paced, growing organization and are energized by building efficient systems, developing high-performing teams, and creating safe, reliable environments, we’d love to hear from you!

Compensation consists of base salary plus bonus. WelbeHealth offers a competitive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match, comprehensive healthcare coverage, and a broad range of additional benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience and relevant qualifications.

Compensation Offering
$120,164.59—$158,617.26 USD

COVID-19 Vaccination Policy

At WelbeHealth, our mission is to unlock the full potential of our vulnerable seniors. In this spirit, please note that we have a vaccination policy for all our employees and proof of vaccination, or a vaccine declination form will be required prior to employment. WelbeHealth maintains required infection control and PPE standards and has requirements relevant to all team members regarding vaccinations.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At WelbeHealth, we embrace and cherish the diversity of our team members, and we're committed to building a culture of inclusion and belonging. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Storage Asset Management is a property management and consulting company that specializes in self-storage. With over 70 years of executive industry experience, SAM employs an incredible team of employees on every level. Voted Best Places to work in PA 2021,2022,2023, 2024, and 2025!

Storage Asset Management is proud to have over 900 employees at the store, regional and corporate office level.

Summary: This position is responsible for overseeing and working with District Managers and Store Managers to maintain their assigned stores in alignment with Capital Improvements and Preventative Maintenance.

Benefits of Joining SAM:

  • A dynamic company with an award-winning culture
  • A clear path for advancement within our thriving company

• Competitive pay with bonus potential

• Paid holidays

• Paid time Off

• Paid maternity and paternity leave

  • Comprehensive healthcare and 401(k) plan
  • Short-Term & Long-Term Disability insurance

• Flexible Scheduling

•Tuition re-imbursement

• Dental Insurance

• Health Insurance

• Vision Insurance

Essential functions of the role that can be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Work closely with the Director of Facilities to address and drive the property maintenance and improvement plans across the managers assigned stores.
  • Work directly with Facility Management team members, District/Store Managers and the property Owners to ensure locations are meeting expectations of property ownership and exceeding when possible.
  • Identification of required Immediate Repairs and ongoing repairs thru new store transitions and current managed stores. Strives to keep repairs on budget thru discussions with SAM teams and Owners.
  • Keeps informed of current and future property needs through timely communications and follow up methods.
  • Ensure all documentation is recorded, filed, and shared appropriately for current and historical reasons.
  • Track info and progress on the current repair ticketing system called MaintainX. This is the single source shared drive for maintenance and capital expenses that are $1000 and above.
  • Ability to work across other SAM departments to communicate and complete repair and capital improvements through completion on approved budgets.
  • Daily follow up with DM, SM and Facility Management Administration for missing information for ownership review and approval.
  • Visit assigned properties for due diligence reviews and for review of outstanding required and suggested repairs for ownership.
  • Coaches store managers on the ongoing repairs, maintenance plans and vendor contracts.
  • Develop asset plans with Facility Maintenance team members to identify, inspect, review and validate past and present maintenance and capital improvements.
  • Work diligently with Facility management team and Field Operations team to develop best practices for maintenance and capital improvement store resource documents.
  • Supports and holds SM/DM accountable for maintenance issues on a proactive plan working within store budgets with proper scopes of work.
  • Identify and celebrate operational successes, as well as develop and implement plans to address opportunities.
  • Creates and strengthens client relationships through ongoing communication and meetings.
  • Communicate effectively with employees, colleagues and customers. To be a positive force for positive and proactive communication across several teams.
  • Willingness to travel to other markets, SAM office in PA, and industry trade shows. Travel approx. 25-30% of time.
  • Valid driver's license is a requirement due to travelling

Qualifications/Education and/or Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor's Degree and previous storage facility experience a plus!
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint and Outlook
  • Past or current understandings of the basics for HVAC and electrical systems is a plus for this position.
  • Demonstrate leadership competency in managing assigned properties in the shared drive data base with all parties.
  • Passion for accuracy for maintenance and capital improvement tasks that are required at properties and seeing those projects thru to completion and budget and on time.
  • Ability to monitor and control expenses. Must understand and work towards correct Scopes of Work so that contractors submit competitive bids the first time around.
  • Must be able to work independently and be a self- starter and task manager.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks on a daily basis is a necessary skill set.
  • Exceptional communication, organization and time management skills.
  • Negotiating ability with vendors is a must. Ability to call on vendors and others to be a problem solver is of utmost importance for this position.
  • Project Management experience is a key skill set in keeping many projects moving at the same time.

Work Hours: In a typical week, this position requires a minimum of 40 hours with regular and predictable attendance. Occasional weekend work may be required.

Work Environment: This work is usually performed with normal noise levels and minimum exposure to hazardous conditions. This is a remote position and may be performed at home. Employees in this position are required to reside in a state where SAM is registered to conduct business.

SAM is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected statuses as required by applicable law.

The Manager, Facilities Transformation & Capital Programs uses facilities spend, robust asset and work order data, vendor performance, and operational trends to identify root causes, shape strategy, reduce R&M costs, improve asset performance, and guide smarter maintenance capital decisions across the company-owned restaurant portfolio.

Reporting to the Vice President, Facilities Management, the Manager leads execution of facilities-related projects from planning through delivery, including maintenance capital governance, program development, stakeholder communication, and results tracking. This role translates insights into business cases and long-range capital plans, including PCI programs that proactively replace critical equipment, reduce R&M and utility costs, mitigate risk, and support compliance. The Manager ensures capital and resources are focused on the right assets, restaurants, and business needs while keeping partners aligned on priorities, risks, decisions, and outcomes.


RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead enterprise facilities performance analysis across spend, vendors, assets, work orders, capital, and operational trends. Identify root causes, recurring issues, cost drivers, risk areas, and opportunities to improve restaurant performance and reduce downtime. Apply root cause analysis to reduce recurring costs, inform targeted training needs, strengthen vendor accountability, and support manufacturer performance conversations that benefit both company-owned restaurants and franchisees.

  • Translate facilities analysis into executive-ready insights, business cases, prioritization recommendations, and decision-support materials that inform leadership decisions, capital planning, vendor performance, and operational priorities. Own enterprise Facilities insights requests, including ad hoc business inquiries where asset, work order, vendor, or performance data can support better decision-making. Use analysis to advance programs that improve restaurant performance, unlock efficiencies, and reduce costs.
  • Own Facilities projects and programs end to end, from planning through execution, closeout, and results tracking. This includes the Proactive Capital Investment program, cyclical facility programs such as roof replacements, parking lots, and paint, and ad hoc installations or initiatives. Through PCI, this role drives proactive replacement of critical equipment and programs that reduce R&M and utility costs, mitigate downtime and safety risks, and support compliance. Establish project plans, timelines, milestones, risk tracking, stakeholder communication, and regular status reporting. Support maintenance capital governance by using asset data, R&M trends, operational risk, and financial impact to prioritize investment in the highest-need, highest-value assets and restaurants.
  • Develop and maintain the Facilities communication strategy for internal and external stakeholders. Ensure clear, timely messaging on project schedules, program updates, process changes, performance insights, and decisions needed to keep partners aligned.
  • Partner across Facilities, Finance, Operations, Development, Procurement, and vendors to connect insights to action, remove barriers, and ensure initiatives are field-ready, financially sound, and operationally sustainable.

EDUCATION QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum: 4 yr Degree in Facilities Management, Business, Finance, Analytics, Construction Management, Operations, or related field.

Preferred: Project Management Professional (PMP), change management, data analytics, or related certification.

EXPERIENCE QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum: 10+ years of experience in facilities management, project management, business analytics, operations, finance, restaurant operations, retail facilities, or related fields.

  • Experience translating data and performance trends into actionable recommendations for leadership and operational stakeholders.
  • Experience managing cross-functional projects, programs, timelines, risks, and stakeholder communication.
  • Experience developing executive-ready summaries, business cases, performance updates, or decision-support materials.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities while driving measurable outcomes.
  • Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving capabilities.

Preferred

  • Experience in multi-unit restaurant, retail, hospitality, healthcare, or commercial facilities environments.
  • Experience with CMMS, work order management systems, Power BI, financial reporting tools, project management tools, or facilities analytics platforms.
  • Experience supporting capital planning, vendor performance management, asset lifecycle planning, or proactive maintenance programs.
  • Experience developing communication plans, stakeholder updates, and change management materials for field or operations audiences.

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Deep facilities management expertise with the ability to connect asset performance, R&M cost drivers, vendor execution, and restaurant operational impacts into practical business recommendations
  • Ability to leverage reporting and analytics tools to identify trends, quantify opportunities, and drive action
  • Strong business acumen with the ability to connect operational, financial, and field impacts into practical recommendations
  • Strong project and program management skills, including planning, scheduling, risk management, status reporting, and follow-through
  • Ability to translate complex data and technical findings into clear, concise, executive-ready communication
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to tailor messaging for executives, Operations, Finance, vendors, and field leaders
  • Ability to build trusted cross-functional partnerships and influence outcomes without direct authority
  • Strong continuous improvement mindset with the ability to standardize routines, improve processes, and create repeatable communication and reporting practices
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and follow-through
  • Ability to manage confidential information and sensitive business priorities with discretion

Yugo is a global leader in student housing dedicated to creating exceptional living experiences for students around the world. With a presence spanning more than 14 countries and 120 cities, Yugo combines innovation, community, and purpose to redefine student living. In the U.S., Yugo operates nearly 40,000 beds across 88 properties in 28 states, delivering vibrant communities designed to support student success both personally and professionally. Guided by its Live Your Best Life philosophy, Yugo fosters sustainability, personal growth, and career development while building an inclusive, collaborative, and forward-thinking culture for residents and team members alike.

The Facilities Operations Specialist plays a critical role in supporting operational excellence across the Yugo portfolio. This role is designed for a highly skilled facilities professional with regional or multi-site maintenance experience who thrives in fast-paced environments and is willing to travel extensively (up to 90%) to support properties during high-need periods.

The Facilities Operations Specialist is a hands-on subject matter expert who partners closely with Area Facilities Managers, site-level teams, and the SVP of Facilities and Development Services to stabilize operations, support turn and move-in readiness, ensure compliance, and elevate maintenance standards across the portfolio. This role balances technical execution with coaching and training, helping develop our on-site Yugoers while ensuring our spaces remain safe, compliant, and welcoming.

This role reports to the SVP of Facilities and Development Services and supports an assigned portfolio of properties nationwide.

Here's what you'll be doing!

  • Lead by example through exhibiting and reinforcing the Yugo Operations culture.
  • Travel extensively to support properties with facilities operations, staffing gaps, high work-order volume, turn readiness, and operational recovery.
  • Support work order completion and make-ready execution to ensure service level expectations are met.
  • Assist with site-level procurement and inventory management, ensuring materials and resources align with budget and operational needs.
  • Conduct property inspections and reviews related to facilities compliance, including operational permits, life safety systems testing, preventative maintenance schedules, and inspection logs.
  • Partner with Area Facilities Managers, Regional Managers, and on-site teams to identify gaps and implement corrective action plans.
  • Provide hands-on technical support across trades, including HVAC diagnostics and repair, plumbing, electrical, and general facilities maintenance.
  • Support development and upkeep of property-specific O&M plans and preventative maintenance programs
  • Deliver timely updates to the SVP of Facilities and Development Services identifying risks, challenges, and opportunities observed in the field.
  • Participate in and support systems training, compliance courses (EPA, OSHA, trade-specific), operations meetings, and company initiatives.
  • Coach and train on-site maintenance teams to improve technical skill, efficiency, and confidence.

Hexium is rebuilding America's isotope enrichment capability by modernizing Atomic Vapor Laser Isotope Separation (AVLIS) into a scalable industrial enrichment platform. To support the next phase of that effort, we're seeking a Senior Project Manager to personally stand up licensed, radiological-grade industrial facilities—creating the infrastructure that will enable the continued development, testing, and maturation of our technology.

As Hexium's Owner's Representative, you'll lead the project from site selection and lease execution through design, construction, and facility turnover. You'll coordinate architects, engineers, contractors, and stakeholders to deliver a facility that safely integrates radiological confinement ventilation, specialized laboratory and manufacturing spaces, and the supporting infrastructure required for advanced laser isotope separation research.

This is a hands-on project management role, not a program management or people management role. Initially, you'll personally lead the core project management work—including site selection, budgeting, scheduling, contractor coordination, site oversight, design reviews, permitting support, and construction management. As Hexium's facility portfolio expands, a team may eventually grow around this role, but success initially depends on your ability to drive projects from inception through completion.


What You'll Do

Site Selection and Lease Execution

  • Personally lead site search and evaluation against facility requirements (floor loading, clear height, power, waste-disposal proximity, zoning)
  • Drive site due diligence with the Hexium legal and executive team; support lease negotiation and execution
  • Serve as Hexium's day-to-day liaison with the landlord throughout occupancy

Design & Construction Management

  • Manage the A/E firm or design-build contractor through all design phases and into construction
  • Serve as Owner's Representative on all construction activities: track schedule and budget, attend site meetings, review submittals and RFIs, manage punch lists, and coordinate final inspections and certificates of occupancy
  • Ensure construction quality meets Hexium requirements and applicable building codes; coordinate with Hexium's QA function on owner inspection activities at key milestones
  • Develop construction and facility budgets and coordinate amongst internal and external stakeholders

Facility Fit-Out for Radiological and Classified Operations

  • Oversee design and installation of the systems used in radiological research.
  • Own MEP scope (power, compressed gas, vacuum rough-pump, cooling water, process drains)
  • Coordinate directly with Hexium's regulatory team so the facility matches license conditions
  • Manage fit-out of laboratory benches, equipment pads, and utility connection points for process equipment; coordinate space planning and floor loading requirements with the equipment procurement team
  • Oversee classified manufacturing area setup, including access control hardware, compartmented workspace, and coordination with security personnel during installation

Commissioning & Compliance

  • Drive punch-list closure and obtain all required occupancy certifications; coordinate radiological baseline survey prior to first material introduction
  • Maintain facility compliance documentation: HVAC filter records, ventilation performance tests, and other building-level records required under the facility's radioactive materials license


Requirements

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, or a closely related field
  • 5+ years of construction project management or Owner's Representative experience, including at least one specialized laboratory, industrial, or controlled-environment facility
  • Direct experience reviewing, tracking, and managing capital project budgets developed by A/E firms or GCs
  • Working familiarity with MEP systems and the ability to coordinate across mechanical, electrical, and plumbing design packages
  • Experience managing general contractors, A/E firms, and specialty subcontractors through construction and fit-out
  • Proficiency with project management tools such as Primavera P6, MS Project, or Wrike
  • Strong organizational skills tracking submittals, RFIs, change orders, and punch lists across multi-discipline projects
  • Security Requirement: Candidates must be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance
  • Export Controls Compliance: This role will be exposed to export-controlled information and requires compliance with applicable export control laws and regulations


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with radiological or nuclear facilities, cleanrooms, BSL-2/3 laboratories, or other controlled-environment construction requiring specialized ventilation and contamination control
  • Familiarity with HEPA filtration systems, negative-pressure ventilation design, or similar confinement ventilation concepts
  • Experience with classified area construction requirements (SCIFs or equivalent)
  • Background in facilities management, including HVAC maintenance programs and building systems contracts
  • OSHA 30 or equivalent construction safety certification
  • PMP, CCM (Certified Construction Manager), or equivalent credential
  • Familiarity with construction within federal complexes and facilities


Physical Requirements & Work Environment

  • Ability and willingness to travel
  • Ability to walk active construction sites regularly, including uneven terrain, unfinished floors, scaffolding, and areas accessed by ladder or stairs
  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods during site walks, inspections, etc.
  • Ability to climb ladders and stairs, and to access elevated, confined, or below-grade work areas as needed to verify construction and MEP installation
  • Ability to wear required personal protective equipment for extended periods, including hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, steel-toe boots, and once the facility is operational, radiological or contamination-control PPE (e.g., coveralls, respirators, dosimetry badges) as required by facility protocols
  • Ability to occasionally lift and carry up to 30 lbs. (drawings, samples, tools, equipment)
  • Visual acuity sufficient to review construction drawings, redlines, submittals, and equipment nameplates/labeling in the field
  • Manual dexterity sufficient for field documentation, equipment inspection, and use of standard office and field technology (tablets, laptops, measuring tools)

Armada is the hyperscaler for the edge, delivering modular AI infrastructure from first deployment to AI factory with speed, scale and sovereignty. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and to the CNBC Disruptor 50, Armada’s solutions are deployed in over 60 countries globally for organizations ranging from energy to defense.

With nearly $500 million in funding to date, Armada is backed by leading investors including Founders Fund, Lux, BlackRock and Microsoft (M12), alongside strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Dell, Palantir, NVIDIA, SpaceX, and Skydio. We are building the infrastructure layer for sovereign and edge AI - rugged, deployable compute for customers that cannot rely on centralized cloud.

Working at Armada means taking ownership, driving autonomy, and delivering impact. You’ll tackle challenges that haven’t been solved before and help build something transformative from the ground up. What you do here will not only define your career but help further Armada’s mission to bridge the digital divide for customers around the world.

About the Role

Armada is seeking a Physical Security – Facilities Lead to own classified design, construction, and accreditation of Galleons for the U.S. Defense sector.

Galleons are built, configured, shipped, and stood up in months, not years. Defense customers need those units accredited as SCIFs, SAPFs, collateral open-storage or closed areas, and related secure processing environments. You will turn ICD 705, DoDM 5205.07, and NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117) physical construction standards into repeatable design requirements, factory and site practices, and accreditation packages that scale with the product line.

You will be the company authority on physical security for secure builds. You will sit with hardware, form-factor, manufacturing, deployment, federal, and security partners from concept through accreditation of the space. Where corporate facility protection overlaps a secure build, you will also set access control, intrusion detection, CPTED, and guard-force requirements as applicable. Corporate physical security is not a separate program. It is in scope only where it touches classified design, construction, or accreditation.

This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role. You will write the standard, walk the line, brief the Accrediting Official, and close the findings. You will exercise independent judgment on problems without precedent, be accountable for results across Armada's secure-build function, and direct the work of contractors, integrators, and cross-functional partners without having direct reports.

Location. United States (Remote). Travel to U.S. factory, integration, and customer sites as needed to support design reviews, construction surveillance, and accreditation.

What You'll Do (Key Responsibilities)

Classified design and construction standards

  • Own physical construction and accreditation requirements for defense Galleons, including SCIFs and SAPFs under ICD 705 and the ICS 705 Technical Specifications, SAPFs under DoDM 5205.07, and collateral open-storage, closed, and discussion areas under 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM).
  • Translate those standards into design criteria, drawing notes, BOM constraints, and factory work instructions that hardware, mechanical, electrical, and manufacturing teams can build to.
  • Lead security design reviews across the Galleon family. Read and redline architectural, structural, electrical, and low-voltage drawings against ICD 705, TEMPEST, and NISPOM.
  • Define perimeter, access-control, intrusion-detection, and video requirements for secure configurations, including door, lock, and wall assemblies, STC and acoustic performance, and inspectable materials.
  • Own TEMPEST and emissions-security design input. Set red/black separation, shielding, filtering, grounding, and penetration criteria, and coordinate countermeasure reviews with customer TEMPEST authorities.
  • Specify Protected Distribution Systems where a Galleon or site requires them and inspect against the applicable CNSSI standard.
  • Build a repeatable secure-Galleon configuration so accreditation is a productized path, not a one-off for every build.

Accreditation and government liaison

  • Serve as Armada’s liaison to Accrediting Officials, Special Security Officers, Facility Security Officers, DCSA Industrial Security Representatives, and customer security staff.
  • Author and maintain Construction Security Plans, Fixed Facility Checklists, inspectable-materials lists, TEMPEST questionnaires, and accreditation submittals.
  • Plan and run construction surveillance, site inspections, and quality assurance on factory, integration, and customer-site work. Hold general contractors, integrators, and internal build teams to the CSP.
  • Drive accreditation from design approval through inspection, remediation, and operational accreditation. Own the punch list.
  • Support capture and proposal teams on DD-254, contract security classification specifications, and physical-security volumes so bids do not promise a configuration that cannot be accredited.

Program execution

  • Own the security workstream on defense Galleon programs. Set milestones, dependencies, and risks against hardware design, factory slot, shipment, and customer required-accreditation dates.
  • Partner with Large Form Factor and Edge Hardware leads, deployment, logistics, and federal mission teams so security requirements are in the design before steel is cut.
  • Stand up the operating rhythm for classified builds: design gates, inspection hold points, documentation control, and lessons learned into the next hull.
  • Author and maintain Armada's internal physical-security policies and standards for classified builds, and mentor engineering, manufacturing, and deployment teams so secure-build expertise scales across the company.

Required Qualifications

  • Active U.S. Secret clearance required.
  • Bachelor's degree and 12+ years (or Master's degree and 8+ years) in physical security, industrial security, or secure-facility construction, with at least 5 years hands-on in design, build, and accreditation of SCIFs, SAPFs, or collateral open-storage areas.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply ICD 705 Technical Specifications to construction drawings and field conditions, not just cite them.
  • Working knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 physical safeguards and of DoDM 5205.07 as it applies to SAPF construction and accreditation.
  • Experience as the technical interface to an Accrediting Official, Cognizant Security Office, or DCSA representative through accreditation.
  • Experience authoring Construction Security Plans and fixed-facility or equivalent accreditation packages.
  • Ability to read construction documents and reject noncompliant details on walls, doors, penetrations, power, grounding, and electronic security systems.
  • Experience with access control, intrusion detection, and alarm monitoring on accredited spaces (UL 2050 or equivalent).
